summary: Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ma earned a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.
Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a scholar in sinology. He studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1952 to 2014.

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1966–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1968–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) worked in tibetology. He studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1972 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, he held posts at Koyasan University (1954, 1965–1967), Nagoya University (1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin (1987), and Shuchiin University (2001).

Yusho Wakahara works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After graduate studies at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami (attested 1982), he taught at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University as assistant professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was attested as Emeritus Professor in 2006.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996). He held posts at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1961–1971), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995).

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1946), Tokai University (~1966–1977), Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka University (~1980–1986).

Yutaka Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2010, studying under Shoryu Katsura, co-supervisor Masaaki Noni, and teachers Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Seio Okuda, Kawasaki held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, training under Louis Renou and W. Norman Brown. He held posts at Kyoto University (1957; 1972–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1975 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history/archaeology, Japanology, and linguistics. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and University of Tokyo, he held posts at Hitotsubashi (1983–2018), Kyoto University (~2006–2020), Research Center for Peace and Reconciliation (2008), and Center of the Tokyo Raids (2019).

Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1969) and earned a doctorate at Rissho University (-1990). He held posts at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin (1895–1976) was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady, and later held a post at Peking University (~1923–1926).

Yuto Kawamura specializes in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), Kyoto University as a postdoc (2015–2018), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a sinologist and philosopher educated at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held academic posts at Tokyo, Saitama, Hitotsubashi, and Daito Bunka universities, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Yün-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later held a professorship at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
